why: Prove the save transaction boundary survives abrupt owned-browser termination and avoid misleading saved feedback during newer writes.
verdict: pass for the exercised interruption and save failure cases
scope: Real worker project put succeeds, transaction deliberately kept open, browser ownership checked using its command line/profile and PID, SIGKILL, confirmed exit, same-profile relaunch. Whole durable record compared before editor opens; checkpoint/view/history compared after opening.
uiFix: Clear old saved toast when saves are scheduled/started; only show explicit Save confirmation if current save status is Saved on this device.
regressions: Real committed save with lost reply reconciled exactly once
Quota fault after body put preserves previous durable record
Unsaved export, retry, reload and Undo
testRefinement: An initial whole-record comparison after opening observed normal editor revision metadata updates. Final test compares whole durable record before opening, then compares editor checkpoint/view/history afterward.
limits: One held project-write phase; not all transaction boundaries
No power-loss, filesystem corruption, physical disk failure or full concurrent-tab acceptance claim
Only explicitly owned disposable profile/browser terminated
